title: Burn-in procedure
text:
Burn-in procedure

  Status:   Template · Not approved  
  Owner:   To be assigned  
  Approver:   To be assigned  
  Last reviewed:   Pending  
  Applies to:   To be defined

!!! info "Before use"
    Complete and approve this document for the applicable platform. Store internal evidence in an approved access-controlled location.

   Approved test plan

Complete this plan before running a sustained load.

  Parameter   Required definition  
  ---   ---  
  Platform and baseline   Hardware configuration and approved version combination  
  Workload   Approved accelerator, CPU, memory, storage, and network coverage  
  Duration and stages   Platform-specific duration, load levels, warm-up, and cooldown  
  Limits   Vendor-supported power, thermal, and health boundaries  
  Pass criteria   Defined stability, error, and performance requirements  
  Stop conditions   Faults or limits that require immediate termination  
  Owners   Operator, reviewer, and escalation contact  

No universal burn-in duration or threshold is specified here.

   Procedure

1. Confirm  validation (validation-procedure.md) passed and testing is authorized.
2. Capture idle health, event logs, configuration, and telemetry.
3. Run the approved staged workload while continuously monitoring health.
4. Record errors, resets, throttling, link events, and performance deviations.
5. Stop on approved abort conditions and preserve evidence.
6. After cooldown, review health and compare before-and-after events.
7. Obtain review and record Pass, Fail, or Incomplete.

   Failure and retest

Record the fault, investigation, corrective action, and retest scope. Require a documented acceptance decision before  onboarding (onboarding-process.md).

Deployment guide

  Status:   Template · Not approved

!!! info "Before use"

   Prerequisites

-     Approved design, change record, deployment scope, and accountable owner.
-     Hardware inventory and  approved platform baseline (../product-engineering/approved-versions.md).
-     Power, cooling, cabling, management access, network, DNS, and time services ready.
-     Approved addressing, storage, access model, and credential handling.
-     Recovery plan, escalation contacts, and evidence location.

   Deployment sequence

1. Record inventory and inspect hardware health before provisioning.
2. Apply the approved firmware and BIOS configuration.
3. Install the approved OS, storage layout, network configuration, and security baseline.
4. Install supported drivers, compute runtime, and required platform services.
5. Configure monitoring, logging, alert routing, and management integration.
6. Record the final configuration and any exceptions.
7. Complete  validation (validation-procedure.md), then  burn-in (burn-in-procedure.md).
8. Obtain acceptance before exposing capacity to provisioning or service consumers.

   Recovery and acceptance

Document rollback triggers, recovery actions, and the accountable decision maker in the deployment-specific plan. Attach the deployment record, validation results, and burn-in evidence to the handover.

title: Onboarding process

Onboarding process

  Status:   Template · Not approved  
  Owner:   To be assigned

  Applies to:   To be defined

!!! info "Before use"
    Complete and approve this document for the applicable platform. Store internal evidence in an approved access-controlled location.

   Entry requirements

-     Deployment record complete.
-     Validation accepted.
-     Burn-in accepted.
-     Exceptions documented and approved.
-     Service scope and support responsibilities agreed.

   Operational handover

1. Assign the service owner, support team, engineering escalation, and coverage model.
2. Register assets, service dependencies, and lifecycle information in the approved system.
3. Confirm role-based access and approved credential storage.
4. Verify dashboards, logging, alert routing, and operational response.
5. Link approved deployment, recovery, incident, and maintenance runbooks.
6. Agree capacity ownership, provisioning controls, and customer-facing handover where applicable.
7. Record acceptance and any time-bound follow-up actions.

   Acceptance record

  Field   Required information  
  ---   ---  
  Service / deployment reference   Controlled record identifier  
  Engineering acceptance   Reviewer, date, and evidence  
  Operations acceptance   Owner, date, and evidence  
  Open actions   Owner, due date, and approved impact  
  Service activation   Authorized decision and effective date  

   After onboarding

Review early-life issues, confirm support readiness, and feed improvements back to Product Engineering and the deployment procedures.

title: Validation procedure
text:
Validation procedure

  Status:   Template · Not approved  
  Owner:   To be assigned  
  Approver:   To be assigned  
  Last reviewed:   Pending  
  Applies to:   To be defined

!!! info "Before use"
    Complete and approve this document for the applicable platform. Store internal evidence in an approved access-controlled location.

   Validation checklist

  Area   Required evidence   Acceptance criterion  
  ---   ---   ---  
  Inventory   Expected server and accelerator inventory   Matches approved design  
  Hardware health   Management-controller health and event review   No unresolved blocking faults  
  Firmware / software   Installed version report   Matches approved baseline or approved exception  
  Accelerators   Detection, device health, and diagnostic results   Expected count and approved diagnostic outcome  
  Network   Link, addressing, routing, DNS, time, and required service checks   Matches approved connectivity plan  
  Storage   Capacity, mounts, permissions, and health checks   Matches approved storage design  
  Security   Access and hardening review   Approved security baseline satisfied  
  Observability   Metrics, logs, and test alert evidence   Events reach the assigned operational owner  
  Functional readiness   Agreed workload smoke test   Approved functional criteria met  

   Execution and evidence

Record each check as Pass, Fail, or Not applicable with a reason, timestamp, operator, and evidence reference. Define platform-specific commands and thresholds in the controlled runbook.

   Gate decision

Do not mark validation complete with unresolved blocking failures. Record remediation or an explicitly approved exception, obtain reviewer acceptance, and proceed to  burn-in (burn-in-procedure.md).

   Release approval

1. Identify the complete platform combination and proposed change.
2. Validate compatibility and run the approved validation, benchmark, and stability tests.
3. Record results, limitations, rollback method, and support requirements.
4. Obtain engineering approval before updating the approved baseline.
5. Communicate the effective date and any retirement or upgrade requirements.

   Exceptions

Record the affected scope, reason, risk, compensating controls, owner, expiry date, and approver in the controlled exception register.

title: Internal benchmarking procedure
text:
Internal benchmarking procedure

  Status:   Template · Not approved  
  Owner:   To be assigned  
  Approver:   To be assigned  
  Last reviewed:   Pending  
  Applies to:   To be defined

!!! info "Before use"
    Complete and approve this document for the applicable platform. Store internal evidence in an approved access-controlled location.

   Purpose

Define a repeatable method for measuring AI infrastructure performance.

   Before testing

-     Confirm authorization, test scope, and isolation from production workloads.
-     Identify the approved platform baseline and test suite version.
-     Define the workload, measurement method, repetitions, and acceptance criteria.
-     Confirm monitoring, evidence storage, and stop conditions.
-     Record configuration and confirm no unresolved readiness faults.

   Execution

1. Capture inventory, software versions, settings, and initial telemetry.
2. Run the agreed warm-up.
3. Execute the fixed workload and parameters for the approved repetitions.
4. Collect raw output, resource utilization, power, thermals, and error events.
5. Record deviations and repeat only under a documented method.
6. Summarize results and variability without discarding unexplained outliers.

   Stop conditions

Stop and investigate hardware faults, unsafe thermal conditions, data integrity errors, or other limits defined by the platform owner. Exact limits must be approved for the hardware.

   Review and publication

Review reproducibility, baseline compliance, and exceptions. Record the decision in  benchmarking results (benchmarking-results.md). Internal raw evidence must remain access controlled.

  Pending   —   —   —   —   —   Not reviewed   —  

   Result record

For each run capture:

- Objective and comparison baseline.
- Server, accelerator count, memory, network, and storage configuration.
- BIOS settings, power profile, OS, kernel, firmware, driver, runtime, and container image digest.
- Dataset or model version, batch size, precision, concurrency, and test parameters.
- Warm-up, repetitions, run duration, and environmental conditions.
- Raw results, summary statistics, variability, errors, and telemetry.
- Reviewer, approval decision, limitations, and evidence location.

   Comparability

Compare equivalent configurations and methods. Explain any changed variable. Separate throughput, latency, scaling, and stability results; include units and measurement definitions.

Follow the  internal benchmarking procedure (benchmarking-procedure.md).
